stem: Where was Gautam a Buddha born?
expl: Gautama Buddha was born in 563 B.C. in the Lumbini grove near Kapilavastu. He attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar) on the night of Vaishakha Purnima. He delivered his first sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) at Rishipattana or Mrigdava (Sarnath) near Kashi, and he passed away at Kushinagar; this passing away is called Mahaparinirvana in Buddhist literature.

stem: Which Buddhist council was not held in Bihar?
expl: The First Buddhist Council was held in the Saptaparni Caves near Rajagriha (modern Rajgir) soon after the Buddha's Mahaparinirvana. The Second Buddhist Council was held in the ancient city of Vaishali. The Third Buddhist Council was held in Pataliputra (modern Patna) under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka. The Fourth Buddhist Council was probably held in Kundalvan, Kashmir. The Fourth Buddhist Council is the only one that was not held in Bihar. Therefore, the correct option is (d).

stem: In which city was the first Buddhist council held during the reign of Ajatashatru?
expl: The First Buddhist Council was held immediately after the death of Buddha in the Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha (Rajgir). At that time, Ajatashatru was the ruler of Magadha. This council was presided over by Mahakassapa (Mahakashyapa), and Buddha’s chief disciples Ananda and Upali were also present. In it, Buddha’s teachings were compiled and divided into two Pitakas—Sutta and Vinaya. Ananda and Upali were considered the authorities on Dhamma and Vinaya respectively.

stem: A Buddhist Council during the reign of Kanishka was held at –
expl: The fourth and final Buddhist Council was held during the reign of the Kushan ruler Kanishka at Kundalvan in Kashmir. It was presided over by Vasumitra, and Ashvaghosha was its vice-president. Here, difficult portions of Buddhist texts were examined properly, and commentaries were written on each Pitaka. Kanishka got these engraved on copper plates and kept them in a stupa. These commentaries written on the Tripitaka are called “Vibhasha Shastra.” It is noteworthy that the First Buddhist Council was held immediately after Buddha’s death in the Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha. At that time, Ajatashatru was the ruler of Magadha. It was presided over by Mahakassapa (Mahakashyapa). The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali about 100 years after Buddha’s death during the reign of Kalashoka. Its president was Acharya Sabbakami.

stem: Where did Mahatma Buddha’s ‘Mahaparinirvana’ take place?
expl: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath. After that, he went to Kapilavastu, Rajgriha, Vaishali and the Kosala kingdom for the propagation of Buddhism. Buddhism was propagated the most in the Kosala kingdom. King Prasenjit of Kosala also became a disciple of Buddha along with his family. While preaching, Buddha reached Pava, the capital of the Mallas. There he stayed in the mango grove of a blacksmith named Chunda. Chunda offered him Sukaramaddava to eat; as a result, he suffered from raktatisara (bloody diarrhoea) and severe pain. Even after this suffering, he reached Kushinara (Kasia), the capital of the Malla republic. Here, in 483 B.C., at the age of 80, he passed away. In Buddhist texts, this event is called Mahaparinirvana.

stem: Tripitakas are the sacred books of the:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Tripitaka is the most important among Buddhist scriptures. After Buddha’s death, his teachings were compiled and divided into three parts; these are collectively called the Tripitaka. These are— 1. Vinaya Pitaka (rules related to the Sangha and a collection of conduct related to daily life), 2. Sutta Pitaka (a collection of sermons delivered by Gautama Buddha and his chief disciples), and 3. Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical doctrines of Buddhism).

stem: Which of the following represents a fundamental difference between Mahayana Buddhism and Hinayana Buddhism?

options.label: c
options.text: Worship of idols of gods and goddesses

expl: Followers of the Hinayana sect of Buddhism were not idol worshippers, whereas in the Mahayana sect, Buddha began to be regarded as a deity and the worship of his idols started. This represents the fundamental difference between the two sects of Buddhism.

stem: Gautama Buddha was elevated to the position of God during the period of:
expl: In the reign of Kanishka, at the Fourth Buddhist Council, Buddhism got clearly divided into two distinct and independent sects—Hinayana and Mahayana. In the Mahayana branch, Buddha was regarded as a deity and began to be worshipped. Along with this, the worship of many Bodhisattvas also started.

stem: The teachers from whom Buddha first attempted to gain enlightenment after the Mahabhinishkramana were:
expl: After the Mahabhinishkramana, in search of knowledge, Lord Buddha reached the hermitage of Alara Kalama and took initiation from him. He practised austerities there, but he was not satisfied. Alara Kalama was a teacher of Sankhya philosophy and was famous for his spiritual powers; therefore, Buddha first attempted to gain knowledge from Alara Kalama and Rudraka Ramaputra.

stem: Which one of the following is not common between Buddhism and Jainism?
expl: Avoidance of extremes of self-mortification (tapas) and sensual indulgence, and the adoption of the Middle Path, is followed only in Buddhism, not in Jainism. However, disbelief in the authority of the Vedas, denial of the efficacy of rituals, and prohibition of violence against living beings are found in both religions.

stem: Nalanda University was a great center of knowledge of -
expl: Nalanda University was world-famous for the study of Buddhist philosophy. Around the middle of the fifth century A.D., during the Gupta period, Nalanda came into existence. Kumaragupta I first donated to the Nalanda Buddhist monastery, and later Gupta rulers such as Buddhagupta, Tathagatagupta, and Baladitya also made donations to the monastery.
